adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Indonesia - Wikipedia
adds.summary: Wikipedia's 'LGBTQ rights in Indonesia' page supplies the national framework the capital stands under and documents Jakarta's raid pattern in detail: police arrested 141 people over a 'gay sex party' in Jakarta in May 2017, detained 144 at the Atlantis Gym sauna on 21 May 2017 (ten charged), and arrested 51 at a Central Jakarta sauna in October 2017 (six charged), all pursued under the pornography law. More recently it records 56 people detained at a hotel in South Jakarta on 1 February 2025, nine detained at another South Jakarta hotel on 24 May 2025, and 75 arrested at a private villa near the capital on 22 June 2025 — offences there can carry up to 15 years' imprisonment. In March 2018 the Jakarta Social Agency declared transgender waria 'socially dysfunctional' and detained trans women in city-run 'rehabilitation' centres unless they signed statements promising not to repeat their 'offence'. Transgender people may change legal gender only after surgery and a judge's approval, and there is no general anti-discrimination law, so police action in Jakarta operates on pornography and morality provisions rather than any LGBT-specific statute.

adds.title: Indonesia: Police must release 75 people arrested in discriminatory raid on "gay party" - Amnesty International
adds.summary: Amnesty International's 24 June 2025 press release responds to the arrest of 75 people in a raid on a 'gay party' at a privately rented villa in Bogor, near Jakarta, and situates it inside the capital's raid series: 56 people were detained for participating in 'a gay party' at a hotel in South Jakarta on 1 February 2025, and nine were detained following a raid on a different hotel in South Jakarta on 24 May 2025. Amnesty International Indonesia's deputy director called the villa raid 'a blatant violation of human rights and privacy' that 'exemplifies the hostile environment for LGBTI people in Indonesia', and demanded the release of those arrested. The release notes that police made the arrests without naming detainees or conducting judicial proceedings, and that those detained risk up to 15 years' imprisonment under Indonesia's broadly worded Pornography Law.

adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Mexico - Wikipedia
adds.summary: Wikipedia's 'LGBTQ rights in Mexico' page gives the state-level legal picture a Quintana Roo visitor stands under: same-sex marriage has been permitted in the state since 2012 (two marriages were performed in Kantunilkín in November 2011, annulled by the governor in April 2012, and reinstated on 3 May 2012 once the state conceded its Civil Code sets no gender requirement), and the state congress legalized adoption by same-sex couples in August 2022. The page records Quintana Roo among the states that enacted legal gender recognition in 2020 and that banned conversion practices on 15 December 2023, and lists the Quintana Roo penal code among hate-crime laws punishing crimes motivated by sexual orientation or gender. It also notes the state ratified the 2011 federal constitutional ban on sexual-orientation discrimination and that Cancún is among Mexico's principal gay-tourism destinations.

adds.title: Quintana Roo y Morelos prohíben las terapias de conversión - Tribuna de la Bahía
adds.summary: Local reporting (Tribuna de la Bahía, 15 December 2023) on the Quintana Roo congress joining Morelos in banning conversion practices: both legislatures approved initiatives prohibiting and sanctioning 'Esfuerzos para Corregir la Orientación Sexual e Identidad de Género' (ECOSIG), commonly called conversion therapies, with penalties of two to six years in prison and fines of 1,000 to 2,000 times the daily UMA (measurement and updating unit) value for those who carry out such practices. This pins the December 2023 reform to a concrete date and gives the sanction levels in force across the state, including tourist corridors such as Cancún and the Riviera Maya.
